source.title: Exponential Convergence Time of Gradient Descent for One-Dimensional Deep Linear Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests gradient-descent convergence on deep linear networks using convergence time and objective suboptimality. Its models and measures differ from the claim versions, which focus on classification error and other specific settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own convergence results for one-dimensional deep linear networks and multi-dimensional experiments. They concern objective convergence, not training classification error, so the rows map to none of the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study proves convergence-time bounds and reports experiments for deep linear product objectives. These results do not test the specified classification, ReLU teacher-student, residual convolutional, activation-matched initialization, stability-threshold, or batch-normalization claims. In particular, initialization-dependent runtime alone does not test V4's signal-and-gradient-preserving initialization comparisons.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors prove exponential convergence-time lower bounds for scalar deep linear networks under specified standard initializations, give a nearly matching upper bound under additional assumptions, and provide evidence that exponential scaling can occur in higher dimensions. They emphasize that this is not a general impossibility result and that additional assumptions or algorithmic changes may avoid it.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies gradient descent on deep linear-network objectives and measures objective convergence time, rather than classification error on benchmarks.
record.method_sensitivity: In the multi-dimensional experiments, the observed depth-scaling pattern differs between Xavier, near-identity variance 1/(dk), and near-identity variance 1/(dk)^2 initializations.

fits_no_version.finding: For scalar deep linear product objectives satisfying the stated assumptions, Xavier and near-identity initializations require exponentially many gradient-descent iterations to reach fixed suboptimality.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient descent can require exponential time in depth on deep linear objectives under standard random initialization, even without spurious local minima.

fits_no_version.finding: For the squared-product objective under Assumption 4, a sufficiently small polynomial step size yields convergence within exp(Õ(k)) times max{1, log(1/ε)} iterations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under specified initialization and target assumptions, scalar deep linear squared-loss objectives admit a nearly matching exponential convergence-time upper bound.

fits_no_version.finding: For the 25-dimensional matrix objective targeting −I, apparent exponential runtime scaling occurs with Xavier and smaller-variance near-identity initialization, but is not observed with near-identity variance 1/(dk).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth-dependent convergence time for some deep linear matrix objectives depends strongly on initialization variance.

record.problems: The multi-dimensional results are experimental and presented in a figure; exact plotted values are not stated in the text. Runs were capped at 10^9 iterations, and the authors say reported means underestimate convergence times when trials fail to converge. The experiments use a specific matrix objective and d = 25.

untested.parts: Training classification error in convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels and model-size or training-recipe comparisons.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks, identity-shortcut comparisons, and the stated tanh and Fixup exceptions.
Activation-matched initializations preserving signals and gradients, their training-speed and trainable-depth benefits, and orthogonal-versus-Gaussian tanh or convolutional comparisons.
Recovery above the initial stability threshold, loss-curvature dynamics, edge-of-stability training, and divergence relative to that threshold.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T2 classification is inconsistent with its correctly unlinked rows. All row states here are relative to the listed claim versions; cannot_determine does not dispute the study's own convergence findings.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, random or corrupted labels, and the stated model-size and training-recipe comparisons.
Teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious local minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual convolutional networks and their training classification errors; the paper studies deep linear networks.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, and the stated tanh and convolutional training-speed comparisons.
Learning rates above a stability threshold, curvature or sharpness dynamics, and the stated divergence comparisons.
Batch normalization's effect on speed, accuracy, and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

rows.subject: one-dimensional depth-k linear neural network
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on F(w) = f(product of the scalar parameters), from Xavier initialization.

conditions.value: i.i.d. zero-mean, unit-variance distribution satisfying Assumption 2

rows.measure: Iterations to reach suboptimality below c0
rows.uncertainty: With probability at least 1 − exp(−Ω(k)) over the initialization
rows.note: The theorem gives an exponential lower bound on convergence time for the stated one-dimensional linear-network objective; it does not measure classification error.
rows.check: The exponential lower bound is correctly reported, but measures convergence of a scalar linear product objective rather than any listed version. Its extracted observed state describes this separate finding.

rows.subject: one-dimensional depth-k linear neural network
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on F(w) = f(product of the scalar parameters), from near-identity initialization.

conditions.value: maxj |wj(1) − 1| ≤ k^−c1 and c2 ≤ product of wi(1) ≤ c3

rows.measure: Iterations to reach suboptimality below c0
rows.note: The result concerns convergence time for a deep linear-network objective, not classification error.
rows.check: The near-identity lower bound is correctly reported but does not compare the architectures or initialization properties named in V3 or V4.

rows.subject: one-dimensional depth-k linear neural network
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on one-half times the squared difference between the parameter product and y.

conditions.value: η = k^−c for a sufficiently large constant c

rows.measure: Iterations to reach objective value at most ε
rows.value: at most exp(Õ(k)) · max{1, log(1/ε)} iterations
rows.note: This upper bound is for the stated squared-product objective and initialization assumptions.
rows.check: An upper bound on objective-convergence time under Assumption 4 does not establish any listed version. It also does not independently establish an exponential lower bound.

rows.subject: d × d linear network
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on one-half times the squared Frobenius norm of the difference between the matrix product and −I.

conditions.value: Xavier; entries independently sampled from zero-mean Gaussian with variance 1/d

rows.measure: Log number of iterations to reach objective below 0.1
rows.value: The text says the figure strongly suggests required runtime scales exponentially with depth.
rows.uncertainty: Mean and standard deviation over 50 trials; the text notes that means are underestimated when trials fail to converge
rows.note: Exact plotted values are not stated in the text. The claim about exponential scaling is the authors' description of the figure.
rows.check: The qualitative exponential-scaling finding concerns a linear matrix objective. Figure 2 reports the mean and standard deviation of log iteration counts among converged runs; capped runs are excluded, biasing the displayed means downward.

rows.subject: d × d linear network
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on one-half times the squared Frobenius norm of the difference between the matrix product and −I.

conditions.value: near-identity; each matrix I + M, with M entries independently sampled from zero-mean Gaussian variance 1/(dk)

rows.measure: Log number of iterations to reach objective below 0.1
rows.value: The text says exponential scaling was not observed.
rows.uncertainty: Mean and standard deviation over 50 trials; the text notes that means are underestimated when trials fail to converge
rows.note: The text explicitly contrasts this initialization condition with Xavier and smaller-variance near-identity initialization.
rows.check: The absence of apparent exponential scaling is correctly attributed to this initialization, but does not measure absence of any listed claim's effect. The figure summarizes log iteration counts among converged runs.
